newsitem.title: PERU: Peru government, rebels end fifth round of talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru government, rebels end fifth round of talks.

text.p: The Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages ended a fifth round of talks on Monday that lasted two and a half hours.

A Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) spokesman, believed to be its leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini, was driven in a Red Cross car from a safe house where he met government negotiator Domingo Palermo back to the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence.
A statement issued afterwards by guarantors overseeing the talks said they were held in a "cordial atmosphere" and dealt with "important issues".

The statement, read in Spanish by the Vatican's representative Archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani and in English by Canada's ambassador Anthony Vincent, added that a sixth round of negotiations would be held on Tuesday.
The third guarantor, Red Cross representative Michel Minnig, was also present at the meeting, along with two government advisers and Japanese government observer Terusuke Terada.
The main sticking point between the government and the rebels is the MRTA's demand for the release of some 400 imprisoned comrades.
